key_insight: A small set of attention heads helps determine whether a multimodal AI follows visual or textual evidence when the two disagree. These “arbitration heads” offer a potential control point for steering that choice at inference time.
problem_solved: When images and text conflict, multimodal large language models may favor a modality that is less reliable for the task, making their answers unpredictable or incorrect.
method: Study how multimodal models choose between conflicting visual and textual evidence.
Identify a small set of attention heads that causally influence which modality drives predictions.
Use these arbitration heads as the basis for lightweight inference-time control; the supplied abstract is truncated before the full method is described.
impact: This work points toward more controllable multimodal systems that can prioritize task-appropriate evidence rather than default modality preferences. The supplied excerpt does not include quantitative results or enough detail to assess practical effectiveness.
visual_elements: Conflict diagram: an image and a contradictory text statement feed into one model.
Attention-head map highlighting the small subset of arbitration heads.
Control dial labeled “visual evidence ↔ textual evidence” to illustrate inference-time steering.
Conceptual before-and-after flow showing default modality preference versus controlled arbitration.
paper_title: Beyond Modality Preference: Controlling Multimodal Arbitration under Modality Conflict in MLLMs
paper_authors: Zhaoying Pan, Shenyu Lu, Jun Hui Wong, Junyi Chai, Xiaoqian Wang
